ai.literal: Those who drink even if they seem like, character those-without friendship, than growing decreasing is sweet.
ai.translation: Even if they show an affection so intense that they seem to drink you up, it is better for friendship with people of no character to shrink rather than grow.
ai.modern: அன்பால் உங்களை குடிப்பவர்கள் போல நடித்தாலும், நல்ல பண்பு இல்லாதவர்களின் நட்பு வளர்வதை விட குறைவதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deceptive affection of people lacking good character. The word 'parukuvār' evokes the image of someone looking at you with such intense, consuming love that they could drink you up. However, if such people have no true moral character, their friendship is dangerous. Therefore, it is much better and safer for such a friendship to dwindle away rather than to grow stronger.

ai.literal: If profitable having befriended, if ceasing abandoning, equality they-who-are-without friendship, even if obtained even if lost what?
ai.translation: What does it matter whether one gains or loses the friendship of unfit people who befriend you when it is profitable and abandon you when it is not?
ai.modern: தமக்கு ஒரு பயன் கிடைக்கும் போது நட்பு செய்து, பயன் இல்லாத போது விலகிப் போகும் தகுதியற்றவர்களின் நட்பைப் பெற்றாலும் என்ன, இழந்தாலும் என்ன?
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against opportunistic friends. The phrase 'உறின் நட்டு' means befriending when there is something to gain, while 'அறின் ஙருஉம்' means abandoning when that gain ceases. The poet calls such people 'ஒப்பு இலார்', meaning they lack fitness or moral balance. Gaining or losing the friendship of such self-serving people makes absolutely no difference to one's life.

ai.literal: Profit calculating friendship-and, payment taking-ones-and, thieves-and, (are) equal.
ai.translation: Friends who calculate their profit, those who offer companionship for a price, and thieves are all alike.
ai.modern: தமக்குக் கிடைக்கும் லாபத்தை மட்டும் கணக்கிட்டுப் பழகும் நண்பர்களும், பொருளைப் பெற்றுக்கொண்டு உறவாடுபவர்களும், திருடர்களும் ஆகிய மூவரும் சமமானவர்களே.
ai.explanation: This couplet equates three types of people who are driven solely by material gain. The phrase 'உறுவது சீர்தூக்கும் நட்பு' refers to friends who constantly weigh what profit they can extract from the relationship. They are grouped with 'பெறுவது கொள்வார்', meaning those who take payment for their company, and 'கள்வர்', thieves. By declaring these three groups 'நேர்' (equal), the text emphasizes that a friendship based on calculation is as deceitful and harmful as outright theft.

ai.literal: Battle midst path will-cut-off untrained horse those-who-are-like than-friends solitude is-best.
ai.translation: Solitude is far better than the friendship of those who are like an untrained horse that throws its rider in the midst of battle.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தின் நடுவே கீழே தள்ளிவிட்டு ஓடும் பழக்கப்படாத குதிரையைப் போன்றவர்களின் நட்பை விட, ஒருவன் தனியாக இருப்பதே மிகவும் சிறந்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares unreliable friends to an untrained horse in battle. Just as a wild horse might panic and throw its rider right when the fighting is fiercest, a bad friend will abandon you in times of crisis. The word 'மா' generally means animal but here specifically refers to a horse used in war. Therefore, the text concludes that facing life's struggles completely alone is much safer and better than relying on such treacherous companions.

ai.literal: having done, protection not providing base people's mean friendship, than attaining not attaining (is) good.
ai.translation: It is better not to attain, rather than to attain, the mean friendship of base people who offer no protection even when befriended.
ai.modern: நட்பு செய்தாலும் பாதுகாப்புத் தராத சிறியவர்களின் தீய நட்பைப் பெறுவதை விடப் பெறாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against befriending base people who are unreliable. The word 'ஏமம்' means protection or security, which is the core purpose of true friendship. 'சாரா' indicates their failure to provide this support even after a friendship is formed ('செய்து'). Therefore, the poet concludes that it is far better never to attain ('எய்தாமை') such a mean friendship ('புன்கேண்மை') than to attain it ('எய்தலின்').

ai.literal: Than a fool's great having-become-intimate friendship, wise people's enmity ten million will be.
ai.translation: The enmity of the wise is ten million times better than the deep intimacy of a fool.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களுடன் கொள்ளும் மிக நெருக்கமான நட்பை விட, அறிவுடையவர்களுடன் கொள்ளும் பகைமை கோடி மடங்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the value of relationships based on the wisdom of the people involved. The word 'பேதை' refers to a fool, and 'பெருங் கெழீஇ' describes an intense, intimate bond. The poet asserts that even the enmity ('ஏதின்மை') of wise people ('அறிவுடையார்') is ten million times ('கோடி') better than such a friendship. This is because the wise, even as enemies, will act with principles and reason, whereas a fool's friendship will inevitably lead to ruin.

ai.literal: Than the friendship of those who are of the joking sort, by enemies ten multiplied by a crore will result.
ai.translation: Ten crore times more good comes from enemies than from the friendship of those who only joke around.
ai.modern: வெறுமனே சிரித்துப் பேசிப் பழகும் தன்மை கொண்டவர்களின் நட்பை விட, பகைவர்களால் பத்து கோடி மடங்கு அதிக நன்மை உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts superficial friends with open enemies. The phrase 'நகைவகையர்' refers to people whose friendship consists only of laughing and joking, lacking true support or sincerity. The poet states that having enemies brings 'பத்து அடுத்த கோடி' (ten crore) times more benefit than having such shallow friends. Enemies, by their open hostility, keep one alert and grounded, whereas false friends offer nothing of substance and can cause unexpected harm.

ai.literal: Possible deed those-who-ruin friendship, without-speaking to-slip let-go.
ai.translation: Without saying a word, let slip away the friendship of those who ruin deeds that are possible to achieve.
ai.modern: முடிக்கக்கூடிய செயலையும் கெடுப்பவர்களின் நட்பை, அவர்களிடம் ஒன்றும் சொல்லாமலேயே மெல்ல நழுவ விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle false friends who secretly sabotage one's efforts. When someone ruins a deed that is otherwise perfectly possible to accomplish ('ஒல்லும் கருமம்'), their friendship ('கேண்மை') is dangerous. The author advises not to confront them or make a scene ('சொல்லாடார்'), but simply to let the relationship gradually slip away and fade ('சோர விடல்').

ai.literal: Even in a dream, it is painful, alas! Action different, word different, those who are - [their] friendship.
ai.translation: The friendship of those whose words differ from their deeds is painful even in a dream.
ai.modern: சொல்லும் சொல்லும் செய்யும் செயலும் வெவ்வேறாக இருப்பவர்களின் நட்பு, கனவிலும் துன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the friendship of hypocrites. The phrase 'வினை வேறு சொல் வேறு பட்டார்' describes people whose actions are completely different from their words. The poet states that having a connection with such deceitful people is painful not just in waking life, but even in a dream. The particles 'மன்னோ' add a tone of certainty and sorrow to the pain caused by such false friends.

ai.literal: in any measure approaching avoid, at home having appeared, in public they who mock - (their) friendship
ai.translation: Avoid entirely getting close to the friendship of those who act friendly in private but mock you in public.
ai.modern: தனியாக வீட்டில் இருக்கும்போது நண்பர்களாகப் பழகிவிட்டு, பலரும் இருக்கும் பொது மன்றத்தில் பழித்துப் பேசுபவர்களின் நட்பை எந்த அளவிலும் நெருங்காமல் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against two-faced friends. The phrase 'மனைக்கு எழீஇ' describes those who appear warm and intimate in the privacy of a house, while 'மன்றில் பழிப்பார்' refers to their tendency to mock or belittle you in public assemblies. The word 'ஓம்பல்' strongly advises the reader to guard against such people. Therefore, one must avoid getting close ('குறுகுதல்') to their friendship ('தொடர்பு') in any measure ('எனைத்தும்').
